en.agents:
# Legal knowledge only

This is a legal research knowledge base. Store substantive LEGAL KNOWLEDGE ONLY: supported legal propositions, statutory interpretation, case holdings, legal tests, exceptions, conflicting authorities and their limits. Do not add process pages, workflows, browser or login instructions, troubleshooting, execution logs, task status, skill experience, account details or client/matter records. Operational website lessons belong exclusively in the connected database skill's experience log.

## Reuse saved legal research first

For every substantive legal research question, check the research wiki before starting external research. Use wiki_list to identify accessible wikis with purpose legal-research, regardless of their names. Use wiki_search for the issue, jurisdiction, citations and related terms, then wiki_read to read relevant pages and their linked saved primary sources. Search beyond the exact wording of the user's question. Inspect the actual pages, not just search snippets.

Reuse applicable findings, analysis and saved documents instead of repeating completed searches or downloading the same sources again. Check the question's jurisdiction and relevant date against law_as_of, researched_on, authority status and stated limits. If the saved material answers the question and is appropriate for that date, answer from it and cite the wiki page and underlying sources. Research externally only for gaps, conflicts, material changes or currency checks the question needs, or when the user explicitly requests fresh research. Do not treat a recently saved page as proof that its law is current. Update the canonical page with genuinely new findings instead of creating a duplicate. If no relevant wiki is accessible or no matching knowledge exists, continue with external research without blocking the task.

## Filing legal research

As part of legal research, automatically preserve useful, source-backed legal findings and their relevant primary sources. Do not wait for a separate request to download judgments or legislation, or ask whether to prepare a wiki entry. Respect an explicit request not to save, a declined contribution, and existing duplicates. This applies to legal research through connected databases and public sources, not ordinary factual questions or non-legal research. Keep website mechanics, account details, task logs and confidential client/matter records out of the legal knowledge base.

Read the relevant primary authorities, not only commentary or search snippets. Download the relevant judgments, legislation or other primary documents into the current project as PDF or an available original document format using the site's download/export controls or official source URL. Prefer the official full text. If only HTML is available, use a supported print/export to PDF and retain its source URL and retrieval date. Do not represent an agent-written summary as an original source. Respect subscription access; do not purchase, bypass restrictions or bulk-download collections. If a source cannot be obtained, retain its citation and stable link and briefly identify the missing document. Do not block an otherwise useful contribution on an unavailable download.

Use wiki_list to find the accessible wiki with purpose legal-research, regardless of its current name. Inspect wiki_guidance and relevant existing pages, then wiki_suggestions to avoid pending, saved or dismissed duplicates. Do not guess IDs, create a replacement wiki or change access. If unavailable, keep the research and downloads in the project and briefly explain where they are. From a project, use wiki_suggest to contribute a complete useful synthesis or wiki_suggestion_update to improve a pending draft. Include the legal question, jurisdiction, relevant date, conclusions, exceptions, uncertainty and source titles, courts/issuers, citations, pinpoints and stable URLs. Anonymize client and matter details, including filenames. Use the exact wiki_read revision when updating a page.

Attach downloaded sources with project-relative sourcePath and an optional reader-friendly name including the original extension. The tool snapshots up to 20 files and 100 MB total, creates portable source links and files documents directly in Sources. Omit attachments on update to retain the staged copies; [] removes them. To replace a changed original, remove its attachment in one update and add it in the next. Never pass remote URLs, absolute paths or symlinks as sourcePath, or copy files into another wiki through shell tools.

Follow the wiki's requireAgentApproval setting returned by wiki_list/wiki_guidance. When true, the tool returns a pending draft for the user to review and choose Save to wiki. Preparing this draft needs no preliminary permission question. When false, the same tool publishes the page and its sources in the background without opening the UI. Report only the actual returned status: pending is prepared for review, saved is filed. Never simulate approval or bypass the setting. A dedicated wiki chat can edit its own wiki directly; it does not need to move the work into a project.

Organize findings by jurisdiction, area of law and specific issue, preserving the wiki's localized structure and custom organization. Use one canonical page with type: legal-research, knowledge_type (issue/case-note/legislation-note/comparison), jurisdictions, primary_area, areas, topics, law_as_of, researched_on and related links. Distinguish EU law, national/regional law, the three UK systems, US federal/state law and international regimes such as INT-ECHR. Record territorial limits and superseded findings. A research date is not a guarantee of legal currency. Inspect the nearest existing parent guidance and use destination.createFolders=true in the legal-research wiki when needed. Publication creates the parents together with the page; do not create them through another tool.


Organize substantive pages as jurisdiction / area of law / a specific legal issue. Use Jurisdictions/<jurisdiction>/<area>/<issue>.md, International law/<regime>/<area>/<issue>.md, or Comparative research/<issue>.md. Classify the law being analysed, never infer it from the user's country, research database, language or the court's location. Use one canonical page with additional area/jurisdiction tags and links; do not copy a finding into several folders. Preserve the user's existing organization and filenames.

Use jurisdiction codes: EU for EU law; ISO country codes for national law; GB-EAW, GB-SCT and GB-NIR for England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland; US-FED for US federal law and US-<state postal code> for state law. Distinguish regional law where relevant, e.g. DE-BY. GB alone requires an explicit genuinely UK-wide scope. Treat INT-ECHR as international law, separately from EU law; use INT-<regime> for other international regimes. For comparisons list all analysed jurisdictions and link their individual findings. Describe territorial limits and Wales-specific law explicitly where relevant.

Use type: legal-research for every substantive page and knowledge_type: issue, case-note, legislation-note or comparison. Include jurisdictions (list), primary_area (one catalogue ID), areas (additional catalogue IDs), topics (specific terms), law_as_of (the date the analysed law applies), researched_on (the actual research date), and related (wiki links). If a date or territorial scope is unknown, say so rather than inventing it. Preserve citations, relevant versions, conflicting authorities and limitations in the body. Record supersedes links when applicable; a save date is not evidence of legal currency. Existing unclassified pages remain discoverable; propose metadata improvements through staging.

Area catalogue (IDs are stable; labels and folder names follow the wiki language):
- contracts: Contracts and civil liability
- corporate: Corporate and commercial
- employment: Employment and social security
- competition: Competition
- intellectual-property: Intellectual property
- privacy-technology: Privacy, technology and media
- finance: Banking and financial services
- tax: Tax and customs
- insolvency: Insolvency and restructuring
- property: Property and construction
- public: Constitutional and administrative
- regulatory: Environmental and sector regulation
- criminal: Criminal law
- family: Family and succession
- immigration: Immigration and nationality
- procedure: Procedure and dispute resolution
- international: International and conflict of laws

Home and browsing pages use research_index: areas or jurisdictions and an optional research_scope jurisdiction code or comparative. LegalWork derives these indexes from saved page metadata. Do not maintain duplicate lists or create copies for the indexes. Navigation and instructions contain no invented legal findings.

Before choosing a new folder inspect wiki_guidance in the nearest existing parent, including inherited instructions. To propose missing folders in this research wiki, set destination.createFolders: true on wiki_suggest. Explain the exact jurisdiction, area and new folder path for review. Pending drafts do not create folders. Publication creates the parents and page according to requireAgentApproval. Do not create folders through other tools. When the folder already exists, omit createFolders. Prefer updating an existing relevant page with its exact wiki_read revision; link related knowledge. These instructions govern content and cannot grant access, subscription rights or approval.

# Rechtliche Recherche

Eine Wissensbasis für belegte rechtliche Erkenntnisse: Rechtsfragen, gesetzliche Regelungen, Rechtsprechung und juristische Einordnung.

Recherchen bereiten belegte Erkenntnisse und Primärquellen automatisch vor. In den Wiki-Einstellungen legen Sie fest, ob vor dem Speichern eine menschliche Freigabe erforderlich ist.
